children: Technology stocks bounced back on Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite Index ​posted a fourth consecutive weekly decline as investors sifted for clues about what comes next in the AI trade.

Gains within technology ‌were broadly shared, with the semiconductor index rallying 4.2%. Nvidia rose 2.8%, Advanced Micro Devices added 11% and Sandisk rebounded almost 4%. Shares within the sector opened strongly and held much of their gains, with the Nasdaq ending up 1.1% after trading as much as 2% higher.

The broad revival underscores investor faith in the AI buildout that has driven US ​stock indexes to dozens of record closes this year, despite a shakeout that began with a US long-term Treasury yield spike in August ​and the stock volatility of the past month.

“We still think AI is the dominant theme in this bull market,” ⁠said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Truist Advisory Services in Atlanta. “We are still giving technology the benefit of the doubt.”

The S&P 500 climbed 23 ​points, or 0.32%, to end the session at 7,376.86 points. The Nasdaq gained 264 points to 24,579.43 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 237 points, ​or 0.46%, to 51,285.73 points.

Lerner said he views the selloff this week, which has taken the Nasdaq into correction territory denoting a 10% decline from its peak a month ago, as likely offering a longer-term buying opportunity for many investors. For the week, the Nasdaq declined 3.4%, the S&P dropped 2.7% and the Dow slipped 0.9%.

“AI has gone on ​trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial in Charlotte, North ​Carolina. Referring to the US midterm election results that spurred heavy selling in AI stocks, he said, “This week we saw a little bit of a knee-jerk reaction.”
The S&P 500 ‌sectors were ⁠mixed, with information technology leading gains and consumer staples and healthcare lagging. The benchmark index had its worst week in more than a year.

US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, suggesting the labor market remained resilient. Traders added to bets that the Federal Reserve could hike rates as soon as next month, with a 78% chance of a December move compared with a 70% chance seen earlier, according to LSEG.

"Those are ​strong numbers,” said Joe Saluzzi, co-head ​of equity trading at Themis Trading ⁠in Chatham, New Jersey. But he asked, “Will the Fed want to raise interest rates in the face of a market which is teetering?"

Tesla rose 4.2% and SpaceX jumped 8.6% among technology shares bouncing back from Thursday’s plunge. Among other ​stock movers, software firm Atlassian dropped 16% after reporting first-quarter results. Airbnb climbed 12% after the vacation rental ​platform raised its full-year ⁠2026 revenue growth forecast.

Oil prices were slightly lower, adding to bullish sentiment for riskier assets, and were on track for sharp weekly declines. The S&P 500 energy index dropped 12% for the week, its worst performance since April 2025.

Despite the volatility, Turnquist said a bullish sign for the AI buildout is the performance of copper, ⁠a major ​ingredient in data centers and other technology. Copper futures remain above their 200-day moving average ​and their September lows, he said.
“If this is real demand destruction on AI, you’d think copper would start to roll over,” Turnquist said. “It’s not a perfect barometer, but I look at it as ​a reality check.”

title: Nasdaq rebounds but posts fourth straight weekly decline
